causal:influence:aadc_activity:positive:.evidence: Manegold C et al., J Inherit Metab Dis 2009 (AADC deficiency: reduced urinary trace amines including tyramine); Brun L et al., J Inherit Metab Dis 2010 (AADC deficiency phenotype: low urinary biogenic amines and trace amines); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (AADC substrate promiscuity: decarboxylation of aromatic amino acids including tyrosine to tyramine) | intervention: AADC deficiency (DDC gene LoF, OMIM 608643): do(aadc_activity=low) -> urinary_tyramine falls
causal:influence:aadc_activity:positive:.mechanism: aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC/DDC) decarboxylates not only L-DOPA and 5-HTP but also L-tyrosine to tyramine (and L-phenylalanine to phenylethylamine); higher AADC activity raises tyramine synthesis from dietary tyrosine; AADC deficiency (LoF) reduces urinary tyramine alongside other AADC-dependent trace amines

causal:influence:abca1_activity:positive.evidence: OMIM 205400 (Tangier disease; reduced apoA-II in severe HDL deficiency); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism; Bodzioch M et al. Nat Genet 1999 | intervention: ABCA1 loss-of-function (Tangier disease, OMIM 205400): do(ABCA1 activity down) -> plasma apoA-II reduced
causal:influence:abca1_activity:positive.mechanism: ABCA1 stabilizes apoA-I on nascent HDL; apoA-II co-localizes on mature HDL alongside apoA-I; ABCA1 deficiency (Tangier disease) reduces HDL particle formation and thus the apoA-II-containing HDL pool. ApoA-II plasma levels are markedly reduced in Tangier disease, though less severely than apoA-I.

causal:influence:abcd1_activity:positive.evidence: Moser HW et al., Neurology 2005;64:1376-88 (adrenal insufficiency in X-ALD, OMIM 300100); Engelen M et al., Lancet Neurol 2012;11:422-34 (X-ALD disease review); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy'; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, peroxisomal fatty acid transport. | intervention: do(ABCD1 loss-of-function) — VLCFA accumulate in adrenal cortex, steroidogenesis impaired, adrenal insufficiency
causal:influence:abcd1_activity:positive.mechanism: ABCD1 (adrenoleukodystrophy protein/ALDP) transports very-long-chain acyl-CoA esters into peroxisomes for beta-oxidation; ABCD1 deficiency (X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy) causes VLCFA accumulation in adrenal cortex zona fasciculata cells, disrupting steroidogenic membrane function and eventually destroying adrenal cortex tissue, causing primary adrenal insufficiency with low plasma cortisol — present in 70-80% of X-ALD patients.

causal:influence:acid_sphingomyelinase_a.evidence: PMID 25803076; (Abstract; Secretory sphingomyelinase in health and disease, Biol Chem 2015); “Acid sphingomyelinase (ASM), a key enzyme in sphingolipid metabolism, hydrolyzes sphingomyelin to ceramide and phosphorylcholine.” | SMPD1 hydrolyzes sphingomyelin to ceramide, so do(SMPD1 up) raises tissue ceramide: acid sphingomyelinase activity --(+)--> ceramide. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:acid_sphingomyelinase_a.mechanism: Acid sphingomyelinase (SMPD1) hydrolyzes sphingomyelin to ceramide; higher SMPD1 activity -> more ceramide generation. This links the acid-ceramidase/ceramide island (acid ceramidase separately degrades ceramide) to the core SMPD1 node via the ceramide-producing reaction.

causal:influence:agt_activity:negative:u.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (primary hyperoxaluria / oxalosis); Scriver's OMMBID — PH1 (AGXT, OMIM 259900) is the canonical hyperoxaluria-causing AGT deficiency
causal:influence:agt_activity:negative:u.mechanism: glyoxylate not detoxified by AGT is oxidised (LDH) to oxalate; reduced AGT activity therefore raises oxalate production and urinary oxalate excretion (hyperoxaluria)

causal:influence:aldehyde_dehydrogenase_.evidence: OMIM #610251 (Acute Alcohol Sensitivity) — ALDH2*2 (Glu487Lys) LoF variant causes elevated blood acetaldehyde and Asian flush syndrome; documented in PMC6804850 (Gene Therapy Correction of ALDH2 Deficiency, Mol Ther Methods Clin Dev 2019) and PMC6875787 (Aldehyde Dehydrogenase Deficiency, Alcohol Res 2019). Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, Ch. 17 — ethanol oxidation pathway: ethanol → (ADH) → acetaldehyde → (ALDH2) → acetate. | intervention: do(ALDH2 activity ↓) via ALDH2*2 homozygosity — blood acetaldehyde rises 5–20-fold after ethanol challenge compared to ALDH2*1/*1 individuals
causal:influence:aldehyde_dehydrogenase_.mechanism: ALDH2 catalyzes the NAD+-dependent oxidation of acetaldehyde to acetate in hepatocyte mitochondria — the rate-limiting step in ethanol catabolism after ADH-mediated ethanol→acetaldehyde conversion. Reduced ALDH2 catalytic activity impairs acetaldehyde clearance, causing blood acetaldehyde to accumulate following ethanol ingestion.

causal:influence:alpha_aminoadipic_semia.evidence: Hyperlysinemia / saccharopinuria (AASS deficiency, OMIM 238700) — elevated plasma and CSF lysine; Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (hyperlysinemia: AASS deficiency causes lysine accumulation); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (lysine catabolism initiated by AASS). | intervention: do(AASS LoF) — hyperlysinemia
causal:influence:alpha_aminoadipic_semia.mechanism: Alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase (AASS, bifunctional lysine-ketoglutarate reductase/saccharopine dehydrogenase) initiates lysine catabolism; its deficiency (hyperlysinemia) abolishes lysine degradation, causing lysine to accumulate in plasma and CSF.

causal:influence:alveolar_surfactant_amo.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-165 (28.4: Fetal Development): 'The lungs begin producing surfactant, a substance that reduces surface tension in the lungs and assists proper lung expansion after birth.'
causal:influence:alveolar_surfactant_amo.mechanism: Pulmonary surfactant adsorbs at the air-liquid interface of alveoli and reduces surface tension, lowering the collapsing pressure and enabling alveolar expansion.

causal:influence:alveolar_ventilation:po.evidence: "if the alveolar ventilation is abnormally low, the alveolar P 2 falls. ... In practice, therefore, the alveolar P 2 is largely determined by the level of alveolar ventilation." — West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 5
causal:influence:alveolar_ventilation:po.mechanism: alveolar PO2 set by balance of O2 removal by blood vs replenishment by ventilation; raising ventilation raises alveolar PO2

causal:influence:angiotensin_II:positive.evidence: "(5) promoting the release of vasopressin." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 16, p 1293
causal:influence:angiotensin_II:positive.mechanism: angiotensin II promotes release of vasopressin (ADH) from posterior pituitary, contributing to volume retention

causal:influence:anp:negative:adh.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-114 (20.5: Homeostatic Regulation of the Vascular System): 'Natriuretic hormones are antagonists to angiotensin II. They...suppress renin, aldosterone, and ADH production and release.' | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-41.5 (41.5: Hormonal Control of Osmoregulatory Functions): 'Its [ANP's] actions suppress the actions of aldosterone, ADH, and renin.'
causal:influence:anp:negative:adh.mechanism: ANP suppresses hypothalamic/posterior-pituitary ADH (vasopressin) production and release

causal:influence:argininosuccinate_synth.evidence: Lehninger, urea cycle step 3 (ASS1); Harrison's / OMMBID citrullinemia type I (ASS1 deficiency) — markedly ELEVATED plasma citrulline
causal:influence:argininosuccinate_synth.mechanism: argininosuccinate synthetase (ASS1) consumes citrulline + aspartate -> argininosuccinate; reduced ASS1 activity (citrullinemia type I) lets citrulline accumulate

causal:influence:aspartoacylase_activity.evidence: Matalon et al. (1988) Am J Med Genet 29:463–471 (Canavan disease: ASPA LoF, elevated NAA); OMIM 271900 (Canavan disease, aspartoacylase deficiency); Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (NAA as ASPA substrate); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (NAA hydrolysis by aspartoacylase). | intervention: genetic LoF of ASPA (Canavan disease, OMIM 271900)
causal:influence:aspartoacylase_activity.mechanism: Aspartoacylase (ASPA) hydrolyses N-acetylaspartate (NAA) to aspartate + acetate in oligodendrocytes; higher ASPA activity consumes NAA. LoF (Canavan disease) abolishes NAA catabolism, causing massive NAA accumulation in brain and CSF.

causal:influence:baroreceptor_firing_rat.evidence: Guyton & Hall — baroreceptor activation of vagal centre; Boron & Boulpaep — parasympathetic cardiac control; BioModels MODEL2101280001 (Schölzel 2015) | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-114 (20.5: Homeostatic Regulation of the Vascular System): 'When blood pressure rises too high, the baroreceptors fire at a higher rate and trigger parasympathetic stimulation of the heart.'
causal:influence:baroreceptor_firing_rat.mechanism: baroreceptor afferents via NTS excite the nucleus ambiguus / dorsal vagal motor neurons, increasing vagal efferent (cardioinhibitory) tone.

causal:influence:bckdh_activity:negative.evidence: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD; BCKDHA/BCKDHB/DBT, OMIM 248600); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 18 (branched-chain amino acid catabolism); Scriver's OMMBID: 3-methyl-2-oxovalerate (alpha-keto-beta-methylvalerate) is the MSUD-diagnostic keto acid of isoleucine (CHEBI:35932 annotated 'clinical marker for MSUD') | intervention: genetic LoF of BCKDHA, BCKDHB, or DBT gene (biallelic mutation; autosomal recessive MSUD)
causal:influence:bckdh_activity:negative.mechanism: The BCKDH complex decarboxylates 3-methyl-2-oxovalerate (alpha-keto-beta-methylvalerate, the transamination product of isoleucine); BCKDH deficiency causes this keto acid to accumulate in plasma — reduced BCKDH activity raises plasma 3-methyl-2-oxovalerate

causal:influence:bckdh_activity:negative.evidence: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD; BCKDHA/BCKDHB/DBT, OMIM 248600); Scriver's OMMBID, MSUD chapter: urine organic acid analysis reveals hydroxylated forms of the BCKA including 2-hydroxyisocaproate; StatPearls NBK557773 | intervention: genetic LoF of BCKDHA, BCKDHB, or DBT gene (biallelic mutation; autosomal recessive MSUD)
causal:influence:bckdh_activity:negative.mechanism: BCKDH deficiency causes 2-oxoisocaproate to accumulate; a fraction is reduced by LDH to 2-hydroxyisocaproic acid (the hydroxy form of the leucine keto acid), excreted in urine — reduced BCKDH activity raises urinary 2-hydroxyisocaproate

causal:influence:bckdh_enzyme_activity:n.evidence: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) OMIM 248600; MSUD GeneReviews NBK1319; StatPearls MSUD NBK557773: 'accumulation of BCAAs and corresponding branched-chain ketoacids of leucine, isoleucine, and valine in the plasma, urine, and cerebrospinal fluid'; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (BCKDH oxidative decarboxylation of BCAAs). | intervention: do(BCKDH loss-of-function) — maple syrup urine disease OMIM 248600
causal:influence:bckdh_enzyme_activity:n.mechanism: The BCKDH complex irreversibly decarboxylates branched-chain alpha-keto acids derived from leucine, isoleucine, and valine catabolism. BCKDH deficiency (MSUD) causes accumulation of BCAAs in plasma, urine, AND CSF. do(BCKDH LoF) -> CSF isoleucine rises.

causal:influence:bckdh_enzyme_activity:n.evidence: Maple syrup urine disease GeneReviews NBK1319; OMIM 248600 MSUD — alloisoleucine pathognomonic, formed by keto-enol tautomerization of alpha-keto-beta-methylvalerate; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, BCAA catabolism (BCKDH); StatPearls NBK557773. | intervention: BCKDH LoF (maple syrup urine disease, OMIM 248600): BCKDH activity DOWN → alpha-keto-beta-methylvalerate accumulates → alloisoleucine produced by tautomerization/transamination → urinary alloisoleucine UP
causal:influence:bckdh_enzyme_activity:n.mechanism: BCKDH (branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase complex) decarboxylates alpha-keto-beta-methylvalerate (from isoleucine). BCKDH LoF causes all BCKAs to accumulate; the BCKA of isoleucine undergoes keto-enol tautomerization and transamination back to produce alloisoleucine (the diastereomer of isoleucine), a pathognomonic MSUD biomarker. Elevated alloisoleucine >5 µM is diagnostic for MSUD.

causal:influence:beta_galactosidase_acti.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID: GM1 gangliosidosis (GLB1 deficiency, OMIM 230500) — galactosylated oligosacchariduria is a hallmark diagnostic finding; Saudubray Inborn Metabolic Diseases (galactosialidosis / GM1 chapter). | intervention: GLB1 loss-of-function (GM1 gangliosidosis): do(beta_galactosidase_activity↓) → urinary galactosylated oligosaccharide excretion↑
causal:influence:beta_galactosidase_acti.mechanism: Lysosomal acid beta-galactosidase (GLB1) cleaves terminal galactose from gangliosides (GM1), keratan sulfate, and galactose-containing glycoproteins. GLB1 LoF (GM1 gangliosidosis / Morquio B, OMIM 230500 / 253010) causes galactosylated oligosaccharides and galactose-rich glycoprotein fragments to accumulate and be excreted in urine.

causal:influence:beta_ketothiolase_activ.evidence: Beta-ketothiolase deficiency (ACAT1, OMIM 203750); Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases; Fukao 2004 Orphanet: C5:1 carnitine (tiglylcarnitine) is elevated in plasma acylcarnitine analysis in beta-KT deficiency | intervention: genetic LoF of ACAT1 gene (biallelic mutation; autosomal recessive beta-ketothiolase deficiency)
causal:influence:beta_ketothiolase_activ.mechanism: ACAT1 deficiency causes tiglyl-CoA accumulation, which is esterified to L-carnitine forming tiglylcarnitine (C5:1 acylcarnitine) detectable in plasma — reduced ACAT1 activity raises plasma tiglylcarnitine

causal:influence:beta_ureidopropionase_a.evidence: Beta-ureidopropionase deficiency OMIM 613161; van Kuilenburg et al., J Inherit Metab Dis 2008 (N-carbamoyl-beta-alanine elevated in urine, plasma, and CSF in UPB1 deficiency). | intervention: do(UPB1 LoF, OMIM 613161) — N-carbamoyl-beta-alanine accumulates in CSF
causal:influence:beta_ureidopropionase_a.mechanism: UPB1 deficiency causes systemic accumulation of N-carbamoyl-beta-alanine that reaches the CNS; elevated N-carbamoyl-beta-alanine is found in CSF of UPB1-deficient patients alongside urinary and plasma elevation.

causal:influence:blood_carbon_monoxide:n.evidence: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-39.4 (39.4: Transport of Gases in Human Bodily Fluids): 'Carbon monoxide has a greater affinity for hemoglobin than oxygen. Therefore, when carbon monoxide is present, it binds to hemoglobin preferentially over oxygen. As a result, oxygen cannot bind to hemoglobin, so very little oxygen is transported through the body… as percent CO increases, the oxygen saturation of hemoglobin decreases.'
causal:influence:blood_carbon_monoxide:n.mechanism: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin with ~250-fold higher affinity than oxygen, occupying heme sites and competitively preventing O2 binding; raised blood CO concentration displaces oxygen from hemoglobin, reducing SaO2

causal:influence:btk_kinase_activity:pos.evidence: X-linked agammaglobulinemia (XLA; OMIM 300755): BTK loss-of-function mutations cause complete absence of circulating immunoglobulin of all classes; Janeway's Immunobiology 10th ed., 'Defects in B cell development and the primary immunodeficiency diseases'; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'Primary immunodeficiency diseases'. | intervention: do(BTK LoF) — genetic loss-of-function mutations in BTK gene; B cell progenitor maturation arrested; no mature B cells, no plasma cells, no immunoglobulin secretion
causal:influence:btk_kinase_activity:pos.mechanism: BTK is essential for B cell progenitor maturation from pro-B to pre-B cell stage; BTK deficiency blocks this transition causing agammaglobulinemia — absent plasma cells of all isotypes and near-zero total serum immunoglobulin.

causal:influence:calcineurin_activity:po.evidence: Jakubowski & Flatt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol I §biochem-4.8.4 (Protein Folding In Vivo): 'calcineurin, an important protein (with phosphatase activity) in immune cells (T cells) required for T cell function'; the FKBP:FK506 and cyclophilin:cyclosporin complexes inhibit calcineurin and thereby prevent T cell activation.
causal:influence:calcineurin_activity:po.mechanism: Calcineurin (protein phosphatase 3 catalytic subunit alpha) is required for T cell activation; its phosphatase activity dephosphorylates NFAT, enabling nuclear translocation and T cell function.

causal:influence:cellular_fadh2:positive.evidence: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-7.4 (7.4: Oxidative Phosphorylation): 'Complex II directly receives FADH2—which does not pass through complex I'; FADH2 is the electron substrate for Complex II
causal:influence:cellular_fadh2:positive.mechanism: FADH2 donates electrons directly to Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase), bypassing Complex I and entering the ETC at ubiquinone

causal:influence:cortisol:negative:plasm.evidence: Glucocorticoid de-novo induction of hepatic TDO lowering systemic tryptophan is established physiology. do() support: Gibney et al., Int J Neuropsychopharmacol 2014;17(6):917-928 (PMID 24472498, verified) shows stress/corticosterone induces hepatic TDO and TDO inhibition raises tryptophan; in humans a hydrocortisone RCT (Hydrocortisone Affects Fatigue and Physical Functioning Through Metabolism of Tryptophan, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2018;103(9):3411) confirms cortisol lowers tryptophan availability via this pathway. Textbook anchor: Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology (glucocorticoid induction of hepatic TDO).
causal:influence:cortisol:negative:plasm.mechanism: Cortisol (glucocorticoid) transcriptionally induces hepatic tryptophan 2,3-dioxygenase (TDO/TDO2) de novo, the rate-limiting, hormone-inducible enzyme of the dominant (>90%) hepatic kynurenine pathway. Increased TDO flux catabolises tryptophan to N-formylkynurenine, depleting the circulating (total) tryptophan pool. The TDO-induction effect dominates net plasma tryptophan, so the sign is determinately negative. Within-scale ORGAN_SYSTEM -> ORGAN_SYSTEM; cortisol is an upstream core variable, plasma_tryptophan is a downstream sink (no new path through the feedback core).

causal:influence:cortisol:positive:intra.evidence: "In the eye, glucocorticoids act to raise intraocular pressure through an increase in aqueous humor production and deposition of matrix within the trabecular meshwork, which inhibits aqueous drainage" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 15, p. 497
causal:influence:cortisol:positive:intra.mechanism: glucocorticoids increase aqueous humor production and deposit matrix within trabecular meshwork → impaired drainage → raised IOP

causal:influence:cortisol:positive:plasm.evidence: "2. Cortisol causes mobilization of amino acids from the extrahepatic tissues mainly from muscle. As a result, more amino acids become available in the plasma to enter into the gluconeogenesis process of the liver..." Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch 77 (chw35), p. 951.
causal:influence:cortisol:positive:plasm.mechanism: cortisol mobilizes amino acids from extrahepatic (mainly muscle) protein stores, raising plasma amino acids available as substrate for hepatic gluconeogenesis

causal:influence:cpt2_activity:negative:.evidence: CPT-II deficiency (OMIM 255110): GeneReviews NBK1253 ('C12 to C18 acylcarnitines, notably C16 and C18:1, are elevated'); Schuler et al. MDPI J Clin Med 2021 (Table of diagnostic markers for LC-FAO disorders) | intervention: loss-of-function of CPT2 gene (CPT-II deficiency, OMIM 255110)
causal:influence:cpt2_activity:negative:.mechanism: CPT2 regenerates oleoyl-CoA (C18:1) from oleoylcarnitine inside the mitochondrial matrix; reduced CPT2 activity causes octadecenoylcarnitine (C18:1) to accumulate in plasma (CPT-II deficiency is characterized by elevated C16 and C18:1 acylcarnitines)

causal:influence:cpt2_activity:negative:.evidence: Carnitine palmitoyltransferase 2 deficiency, OMIM:255110 — LoF causes accumulation of long-chain acylcarnitines (C16, C18) in plasma (hallmark of newborn screening)
causal:influence:cpt2_activity:negative:.mechanism: RHEA:12661 (EC 2.3.1.21), physiological direction reversed: O-hexadecanoyl-(R)-carnitine (palmitoylcarnitine) + CoA = hexadecanoyl-CoA + (R)-carnitine; CPT2 cleaves acylcarnitines back to acyl-CoA inside mitochondria; palmitoylcarnitine is the substrate

causal:influence:cpt2_activity:negative:.evidence: CPT II deficiency (myopathic form), OMIM 255110. The commonest inherited cause of recurrent exertional rhabdomyolysis; episodic myoglobinuria and CK elevation provoked by prolonged exercise, fasting or intercurrent illness. Harrison's "Metabolic Myopathies" / "Rhabdomyolysis". Leak panel curated above. *** DRAFT prototype ***
causal:influence:cpt2_activity:negative:.mechanism: CPT II enables mitochondrial long-chain fatty-acid oxidation, the main fuel for sustained exercise and fasting; LoF starves the myocyte of ATP during prolonged exertion/fasting, failing the sarcolemmal pumps and damaging the membrane (quality: CPT2 activity → disposition: fatty-acid-oxidation ATP capacity → process: prolonged-exertion/fasting energy failure / membrane injury → quality: sarcolemmal permeability). Gated by prolonged exercise, fasting or fever.

causal:influence:csf_tetrahydrobiopterin.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (tyrosine hydroxylase requires BH4); Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (BH4-synthesis defects: low CSF HVA and 5-HIAA)
causal:influence:csf_tetrahydrobiopterin.mechanism: BH4 is the obligatory cofactor of tyrosine hydroxylase, the rate-limiting step converting tyrosine to L-DOPA; reduced BH4 lowers DOPA/dopamine synthesis (BH4-deficiency states show low CSF HVA)

causal:influence:cyp21a2_activity:positi.evidence: 21-hydroxylase deficiency (congenital adrenal hyperplasia), OMIM:201910 — LoF causes decreased 11-deoxycortisol (and consequently cortisol) synthesis
causal:influence:cyp21a2_activity:positi.mechanism: RHEA:50308 (EC 1.14.15.15): 17alpha-hydroxyprogesterone + reduced [NADPH--hemoprotein reductase] + O2 = 11-deoxycortisol + oxidized [NADPH--hemoprotein reductase] + H2O + H(+); 11-deoxycortisol is the product

causal:influence:duodenal_chyme_acidity:.evidence: StatPearls: Physiology, Secretin (NBK537116) — 'S-cells located in the duodenum and proximal jejunum secrete secretin in response to increased [H+] in the lumen'; Pearson A&P: 'A drop in pH below 4.5 in the duodenum stimulates the secretion of secretin'; Johnson & Grossman, Advances in Physiology Education 2009 (doi:10.1152/advan.00023.2009) — classical paper establishing duodenal acidification as the primary secretin stimulus. | intervention: do(duodenal_chyme_acidity↑) — as occurs when gastric acid hypersecretion (e.g. Zollinger-Ellison syndrome) delivers very acidic chyme to the duodenum, or experimentally by intraduodenal HCl infusion
causal:influence:duodenal_chyme_acidity:.mechanism: Acidic duodenal chyme (pH < 4.5 entering the duodenum from the stomach) directly stimulates intestinal S-cells via luminal H+ sensing, triggering secretin secretion into the portal circulation. This is the canonical stimulus-secretion coupling for secretin release.

causal:influence:echs1_activity:negative.evidence: ECHS1 deficiency (Leigh syndrome with valine/isoleucine catabolism block), OMIM:616277 — LoF causes elevated plasma tiglylcarnitine (C5:1), the characteristic newborn-screening and plasma acylcarnitine marker
causal:influence:echs1_activity:negative.mechanism: RHEA:26558 (EC 4.2.1.17): (3S)-3-hydroxybutanoyl-CoA = (2E)-butenoyl-CoA + H2O; physiological direction is hydration of (2E)-enoyl-CoA to (3S)-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA; tiglyl-CoA (2-methylcrotonoyl-CoA, the isoleucine catabolism intermediate) is an ECHS1 substrate; plasma tiglylcarnitine (O-tiglylcarnitine, CHEBI:71179) is the measurable acylcarnitine surrogate

causal:influence:elovl6_activity:positiv.evidence: Matsuzaka et al. (2002) J Lipid Res 43:911-920 (ELOVL6 mRNA co-induced with FAS/SCD1 by insulin/SREBP-1c); Nobuyuki et al. PMC4242452 — Elovl6 KO blocks stearate/oleate synthesis; Ohno et al. PMC7790921 (Role of fatty acid elongase Elovl6 in energy metabolism); Wakana et al. 2015 (de novo lipogenesis reduction in ELOVL6 KO liver). Inborn error of fatty acid elongation (ELOVL6 LoF) markedly reduces elongation of palmitate to stearate and the overall de novo lipogenic product profile. | intervention: genetic LoF of ELOVL6 (elongase deficiency): hepatic de novo lipogenesis rate falls; ELOVL6 overexpression: lipogenesis increases
causal:influence:elovl6_activity:positiv.mechanism: ELOVL6 is the rate-limiting elongase in hepatic de novo lipogenesis, catalysing the SREBP-1c-regulated chain elongation of palmitate (C16:0) to stearate (C18:0). As a lipogenic enzyme co-regulated with FAS and SCD1, ELOVL6 activity is a direct determinant of the de novo lipogenic flux; ELOVL6 knockout reduces hepatic C18 fatty acid production and blunts de novo lipogenesis.

causal:influence:erythroblast_maturation.evidence: Chasis & Mohandas (2008) Blood 112:470-478, PMID 18650462 (central macrophage ingests extruded nuclei); Manwani & Bieker (2008) Curr Top Dev Biol 82:23-53, PMID 18282516. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:erythroblast_maturation.mechanism: erythroblast enucleation releases pyrenocytes (extruded nuclei) presenting phosphatidylserine, engaging macrophage clearance receptors that reinforce the nurse program (quality: erythroblast maturation/enucleation rate -> disposition: PS exposure + ICAM4-alphaV contact -> process: GO:0006911 phagocytosis of pyrenocytes -> quality: macrophage support activity)

causal:influence:estradiol:positive:plas.evidence: "Estrogen increases TBG by mechanisms already mentioned." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 11, p. 354
causal:influence:estradiol:positive:plas.mechanism: estrogen increases hepatic TBG sialylation and plasma half-life, raising TBG concentration

causal:influence:estradiol:positive:uter.evidence: PMID 19589861; (Abstract); “estradiol was able to activate the PI3K/mTOR signaling pathway in uterine myocytes and suggest that this activation is responsible for the induction of myometrial hyperplasia during early gestation.” | Estradiol induces myometrial hyperplasia, supporting do(estradiol up) -> myometrial (uterine smooth muscle) mass up (+). [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:estradiol:positive:uter.mechanism: estradiol -> ER -> IGF1/PI3K/mTOR activation in uterine myocytes -> myometrial hyperplasia -> increased uterine smooth muscle mass

causal:influence:fgf23:negative:parathyr.evidence: "FGF23, an important phosphate-regulating hormone ... activates FGF receptor 1 and its coreceptor, Klotho, on parathyroid cells and thereby suppresses PTH synthesis" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 29 (PTH Biosynthesis), p 1202
causal:influence:fgf23:negative:parathyr.mechanism: FGF23 activates FGFR1 + Klotho on parathyroid chief cells (quality: plasma FGF23 → disposition: FGFR1/Klotho signalling → process: suppression of PTH synthesis/secretion → quality: chief-cell PTH secretion rate)

causal:influence:free_t3:negative:parasy.evidence: "Tachycardia is virtually always present and is due to a combination of increased sympathetic and decreased vagal tone." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 12, p. 365
causal:influence:free_t3:negative:parasy.mechanism: Excess thyroid hormones decrease cardiac vagal (parasympathetic) tone, contributing to tachycardia in thyrotoxicosis

causal:influence:free_t4:positive:restin.evidence: "Resting energy expenditure correlates very well with the free T4 and TSH in hypothyroid patients given varying doses of exogenous levothyroxine." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 11, p. 360  ||  "An excess of thyroid hormone as seen in thyrotoxicosis leads to increased resting energy expenditure that in many individuals will lead to significant weight loss" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 40, p 1570
causal:influence:free_t4:positive:restin.mechanism: thyroid hormone sets metabolic rate; dose-graded exogenous levothyroxine in hypothyroid patients raises resting energy expenditure proportionally

causal:influence:fructose_1_6_bisphospha.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 15 (gluconeogenesis: FBP1 is the key regulatory step, hydrolyzes F1,6-BP → F6P; flux-controlling enzyme); Scriver's OMMBID (FBP1 deficiency, OMIM 229700: fasting hypoglycemia + lactic acidosis in neonates/infants); Harrison's Principles (gluconeogenic enzyme deficiencies — FBP1). | intervention: FBP1 loss-of-function (FBP1 deficiency, OMIM 229700): do(fructose_1_6_bisphosphatase_activity↓) → gluconeogenesis blocked → fasting plasma glucose↓
causal:influence:fructose_1_6_bisphospha.mechanism: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase 1 (FBP1) catalyzes the irreversible hydrolysis of fructose-1,6-bisphosphate to fructose-6-phosphate in gluconeogenesis, a committed rate-controlling step. FBP1 LoF (FBP1 deficiency, OMIM 229700) → gluconeogenesis blocked → fasting hypoglycemia (plasma glucose falls) with lactic acidosis (lactate cannot be converted to glucose). FBP1 activity ↑ → gluconeogenic flux ↑ → hepatic glucose production ↑ → plasma glucose ↑.

In GLA deficiency (Fabry disease), Gb3 accumulates in plasma, urine, and lysosomes of multiple cell types. More GLA activity keeps plasma Gb3 low.

causal:influence:glycerol_kinase_activit.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 17 (glycerol-3-phosphate from adipose lipolysis: GK phosphorylates glycerol; hepatic glycerol kinase is essential for glycerol utilization in gluconeogenesis); Scriver's OMMBID (glycerol kinase deficiency, OMIM 307030: X-linked isolated GK deficiency — hypertriglyceridemia + glycerolemia + glyceroluria from inability to phosphorylate plasma glycerol); Harrison's Principles (glycerol kinase deficiency — pseudohypertriglyceridaemia from accumulated glycerol). | intervention: GK loss-of-function (glycerol kinase deficiency, OMIM 307030): do(glycerol_kinase_activity↓) → plasma glycerol accumulates (glycerolemia)
causal:influence:glycerol_kinase_activit.mechanism: Glycerol kinase (GK) phosphorylates free glycerol to glycerol-3-phosphate, committing it to glycolysis (via DHAP) or to phospholipid/triacylglycerol synthesis. GK is the principal route for clearance of circulating glycerol in liver, intestine, and adipose tissue. GK LoF (glycerol kinase deficiency, OMIM 307030) → glycerol cannot be phosphorylated → plasma glycerol accumulates (glycerolemia/glyceroluria is the diagnostic marker). GK activity ↑ → glycerol cleared → plasma glycerol ↓.

causal:influence:haao_activity:positive:.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, kynurenine pathway (3-HAO step to quinolinate); Bender DA, Biochem J 1989 (tryptophan → quinolinate via 3-HAO); OMIM 604521 HAAO gene. | intervention: HAAO activity change: do(HAAO UP) → urinary quinolinate UP; do(HAAO DOWN) → urinary quinolinate DOWN
causal:influence:haao_activity:positive:.mechanism: HAAO (3-hydroxyanthranilate 3,4-dioxygenase) converts 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid → alpha-amino-beta-carboxymuconate semialdehyde, which spontaneously cyclizes to quinolinate. More HAAO activity → more quinolinate produced; HAAO LoF blocks quinolinate synthesis so urinary quinolinate falls.

causal:influence:hepcidin:positive:ferri.evidence: Nemeth et al. 2004 Science 306:2090 (PMID 15514116); Masison2022 BioModels MODEL2211030002 (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0281401) [citations PubMed-verified]

causal:influence:hibch_activity:negative.evidence: HIBCH deficiency (OMIM 250620): urinary metabolite investigations show increased 2,3-dihydroxy-2-methylbutyrate as a diagnostic marker indicating methacrylyl-CoA accumulation — Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases; Ferdinandusse et al., J Inherit Metab Dis 2015 (PMID 26163321: metabolite studies in HIBCH defects, increases in 2,3-dihydroxy-2-methylbutyrate) | intervention: HIBCH loss-of-function (3-hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA hydrolase deficiency) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:hibch_activity:negative.mechanism: 3-Hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA hydrolase (HIBCH) cleaves 3-hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA to free 3-hydroxyisobutyrate and CoA in valine catabolism; HIBCH deficiency causes 3-hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA to accumulate and back up to methacrylyl-CoA (a reactive electrophile), which undergoes conjugation reactions producing 2,3-dihydroxy-2-methylbutyrate as a urinary shunt metabolite — reduced HIBCH activity raises urinary 2,3-dihydroxy-2-methylbutyrate

Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 2005;102:2129–2134, increased hypothalamic GPR54 signaling in primates reactivates GnRH pulse generator)

causal:influence:intracellular_atp:negat.evidence: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-7.7 (7.7: Regulation of Cellular Respiration): 'If either acetyl groups or NADH accumulates, there is less need for the reaction, and the rate decreases.' Table 7.1 lists ATP, NADH as decreasing pyruvate dehydrogenase.

causal:influence:intracellular_calcium:p.mechanism: a rise in cytoplasmic Ca2+ is the major trigger for smooth muscle contraction

causal:influence:intracranial_pressure:p.evidence: StatPearls: Cushing Reflex (NBK549801) — 'The mechanism of this reflex is stimulation of sympathetic neurons in the medulla by brainstem compression... causing peripheral vasoconstriction and an increase in cardiac output, which serve to increase arterial blood pressure'; PMC5809772 — 'Intracranial Pressure Is a Determinant of Sympathetic Activity'; Wikipedia: Cushing reflex — characteristic Cushing triad (hypertension, bradycardia, irregular respiration). | intervention: do(intracranial_pressure↑) — as occurs in traumatic brain injury, subarachnoid hemorrhage, hydrocephalus, intracranial mass; clinically correlates with the Cushing triad sign of impending brainstem herniation
causal:influence:intracranial_pressure:p.mechanism: Cushing reflex: acute elevation of intracranial pressure (ICP) compresses the brainstem and medullary vasomotor centers, activating the sympathetic nervous system, causing peripheral vasoconstriction and increased cardiac output → systemic hypertension. The purpose is to maintain cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP = MAP − ICP); rising ICP obligately drives MAP upward to preserve CPP.

causal:influence:isovaleryl_coa_dehydrog.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray — isovaleric acidemia (IVD, OMIM 243500): urinary isovalerylglycine is the diagnostic marker
causal:influence:isovaleryl_coa_dehydrog.mechanism: IVD dehydrogenates isovaleryl-CoA in leucine catabolism; deficiency accumulates isovaleryl-CoA, conjugated with glycine to isovalerylglycine (the most reliable marker) — reduced IVD activity raises it

causal:influence:lepr_signaling:negative.evidence: INTERVENTIONAL (genetic). Leptin/LEPR deficiency disinhibits AgRP/NPY orexigenic drive; recombinant leptin restores it. DRAFT for domain review.

causal:influence:leptin:positive:periphe.mechanism: central leptin signalling via hypothalamic circuits increases peripheral glucose disposal into muscle and brown adipose tissue

causal:influence:lh:positive:luteal_prog.evidence: "The hCG secreted by the trophoblast acts as a surrogate LH and prevents regression of the corpus luteum that provides a continuous supply of progesterone until the placental tissue starts to produce sufficient quantities of progesterone." — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 17 (luteal phase / corpus luteum maintenance)
causal:influence:lh:positive:luteal_prog.mechanism: LH/hCG acts on luteal-cell LHCGR (quality: plasma LH → disposition: LHCGR/cAMP signalling → process: corpus luteum maintenance + steroidogenesis → quality: luteal-cell progesterone secretion rate); hCG (surrogate LH) rescues the corpus luteum in early pregnancy

causal:influence:lias_activity:positive:.evidence: Hyperglycinemia, lactic acidosis, and seizures (HGCLAS) OMIM 614462 (LIAS biallelic LoF); PMC3234378 lipoic acid synthetase deficiency (neonatal epilepsy, defective mitochondrial energy metabolism); Mayr et al. JIMD 2014 PMID 24777537 (lipoic acid biosynthesis defects); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (lipoic acid as prosthetic group of pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase). | intervention: LIAS biallelic loss-of-function (OMIM 614462): tissue lipoic acid content falls, mitochondrial enzyme complexes lose cofactor [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:lias_activity:positive:.mechanism: LIAS (lipoyl synthase, mitochondrial) catalyzes the final step of de novo lipoic acid biosynthesis in mitochondria, inserting two sulfur atoms into the octanoyl precursor chain attached to lipoyl carrier proteins. LIAS loss-of-function abolishes endogenous lipoic acid synthesis, causing hyperglycinemia, lactic acidosis, and seizures (HGCLAS) and severely reducing tissue lipoic acid content including in skeletal muscle.

causal:influence:lung_compliance:negativ.evidence: "a low surface tension in the alveoli increases the compliance of the lung and reduces the work of expanding it with each breath" (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 7)
causal:influence:lung_compliance:negativ.mechanism: lowering surface tension raises compliance and reduces the work of expanding the lung each breath; reduced compliance (stiff lungs) increases elastic work of breathing

Adenosine/A1 is a required constituent of JGA/tubuloglomerular-feedback signaling (Sun, Samuelson, Yang, Huang, Paliege, Saunders, Briggs & Schnermann, PNAS 2001;98(17):9983-9988, PMID:11504952, opened; note: Sun 2001 establishes the adenosine/A1-dependence of TGF, the elevated-plasma-renin result is Brown 2001). Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (high distal NaCl suppresses renin); OmniPath ADORA1 Gi-coupled is_inhibition. | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-148 (25.5: Microscopic Anatomy of the Kidney): 'A second function of the macula densa cells is to regulate renin release from the juxtaglomerular cells of the afferent arteriole.'; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-41.2 (41.2: The Kidneys and Osmoregulatory Organs): 'The JGC is an endocrine structure that secretes the enzyme renin and the hormone erythropoietin. When hormones trigger the macula densa cells in the DCT due to variations in blood volume, blood pressure, or electrolyte balance, these cells can immediately communicate the problem to the capillaries in the afferent and efferent arterioles.' Macula densa senses luminal NaCl and signals JG granular cells to regulate renin secretion. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:macula_densa_nacl_signa.mechanism: macula densa basolateral ATP release (pannexin-1/P2) -> ecto-5'-nucleotidase -> adenosine -> ADORA1 (A1 adenosine receptor, Gi) on JG granular cell -> down-regulates cAMP/PKA -> inhibits renin exocytosis (GO:0002001 renin secretion into blood, negatively regulated)

causal:influence:macula_densa_nacl_signa.evidence: "Decreased Macula Densa Sodium Chloride Causes Dilation of Afferent Arterioles ... it decreases resistance to blood flow in the afferent arterioles, which raises glomerular hydrostatic pressure" -- Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch 26 (Urine Formation I), Fig 26-18, p 324
causal:influence:macula_densa_nacl_signa.mechanism: increased distal NaCl at macula densa -> ATP/adenosine release -> afferent arteriolar constriction -> raised afferent resistance (tubuloglomerular feedback); decreased NaCl dilates the afferent arteriole

causal:influence:malonyl_coa_level:negat.mechanism: Malonyl-CoA (product of ACC/de novo lipogenesis) allosterically inhibits CPT1, blocking fatty-acid translocation into mitochondria and thus β-oxidation

causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.evidence: Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases; GeneReviews MCAD deficiency (ACADM, OMIM 201450): diagnostic acylcarnitine / urinary organic-acid profiling includes C10:2 acylcarnitine species when MCAD is deficient; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 17 (beta-oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids) | intervention: MCAD deficiency (ACADM loss-of-function, OMIM 201450)

Ch.32 (Red Blood Cells, Anemia, and Polycythemia) §Role of the Kidneys in Formation of Erythropoietin: “both norepinephrine and epinephrine and several of the prostaglandins stimulate erythropoietin production”
causal:influence:norepinephrine:positive.mechanism: catecholamine signalling stimulates renal erythropoietin secretion independent of renal hypoxia

causal:influence:nsdhl_activity:negative.evidence: Konig A et al. Am J Hum Genet. 2000;66:1210-1218 (NSDHL mutations in CHILD syndrome; monomethylsterol and C4-sterol accumulation); OMIM 308050 (CHILD syndrome, X-linked); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, demethylation of methylsterols | intervention: NSDHL loss-of-function (CHILD syndrome, OMIM 308050): do(NSDHL activity down) -> plasma monomethylsterol up

causal:influence:opioid_concentration:ne.evidence: "Administration of opioid antagonists such as naloxone or naltrexone results in an increase in LH pulse frequency in normal men, suggesting that endogenous opioid neuronal systems within the hypothalamus exert a negative regulation on pulsatile GnRH secretion. Therefore, exogenous administration of opioids most likely causes reduced gonadotropin secretion by suppressing hypothalamic GnRH secretion." — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 19, p. 732
causal:influence:opioid_concentration:ne.mechanism: exogenous opioids suppress hypothalamic GnRH secretion via mu-opioid receptors; opioid antagonist naloxone/naltrexone increases LH pulse frequency, confirming endogenous opioid inhibitory tone on GnRH

causal:influence:ornithine_aminotransfer.evidence: Gyrate atrophy (OAT deficiency, OMIM 258870): Valle & Simell (2001) in Scriver's OMMBID (OAT reaction: ornithine + alpha-KG -> P5C + glutamate, consumes alpha-KG); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (OAT as mitochondrial aminotransferase using alpha-KG); Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (OAT deficiency: hyperornithinemia, impaired P5C/glutamate/proline synthesis). Intervention: do(OAT LoF). | intervention: genetic loss-of-function of OAT (gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina, OMIM 258870)
causal:influence:ornithine_aminotransfer.mechanism: Ornithine aminotransferase (OAT) catalyzes the reversible transamination of L-ornithine using alpha-ketoglutarate as the amino-acceptor: ornithine + alpha-KG -> pyrroline-5-carboxylate (P5C) + glutamate, consuming alpha-KG. Active OAT depletes the alpha-KG pool; OAT deficiency (gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina, OMIM 258870) spares alpha-KG from this transamination, allowing the CSF alpha-KG pool to rise. The reciprocal: do(OAT LoF) -> elevated ornithine AND elevated alpha-KG.

causal:influence:pdh_complex_activity:ne.evidence: Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (PDH complex deficiency — markedly elevated CSF and plasma alanine is a hallmark; pyruvate-to-alanine transamination by ALT); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (alanine aminotransferase, ALT; pyruvate is the alanine backbone); PDH complex deficiency OMIM 312170. | intervention: do(PDHA1 LoF) — PDH complex deficiency
causal:influence:pdh_complex_activity:ne.mechanism: PDH complex deficiency causes pyruvate accumulation; alanine aminotransferase (ALT) transamination of pyruvate + glutamate -> alanine + alpha-ketoglutarate is driven to produce excess alanine; PDH deficiency is the canonical cause of hyperalaninemia in CSF.

causal:influence:phosphomannomutase_acti.evidence: OMIM 212065 (PMM2-CDG / CDG-Ia: coagulopathy including reduced antithrombin III documented as clinical feature). Bhatt et al. 2023 J Thromb Haemost (PMID 37224763) 'Coagulation abnormalities in a prospective cohort of 50 patients with PMM2-CDG' (antithrombin among coagulation proteins reduced in PMM2-CDG). Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (N-glycosylation: PMM2 -> mannose-1-P -> GDP-mannose -> dolichol-PP-oligosaccharide assembly). Intervention: do(PMM2 LoF, PMM2-CDG, OMIM 212065) -> GDP-mannose deficiency -> hypoglycosylation of SERPINC1 -> antithrombin activity DOWN. | intervention: do(PMM2 LoF, PMM2-CDG/CDG-Ia, OMIM 212065) -> GDP-mannose deficiency -> N-glycosylation defect of antithrombin (SERPINC1) -> antithrombin anticoagulant activity DOWN [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:phosphomannomutase_acti.mechanism: PMM2 (phosphomannomutase 2) converts mannose-6-phosphate to mannose-1-phosphate, the precursor for GDP-mannose synthesis, which is essential for N-linked glycosylation. PMM2 LoF (PMM2-CDG / CDG-Ia, OMIM 212065) causes global N-glycosylation deficiency. Antithrombin III (SERPINC1) is an N-glycosylated serine protease inhibitor; its anticoagulant activity and plasma half-life depend on intact N-glycosylation. In PMM2-CDG patients, approximately 20% of antithrombin molecules have N-glycosylation defects, reducing functional antithrombin activity -> coagulopathy/thrombophilia. PMM2 activity UP -> adequate GDP-mannose -> complete N-glycosylation of antithrombin -> normal antithrombin activity.

causal:influence:pituitary_gh:positive:p.evidence: "Both IGFBP3 and ALS are GH dependent" and "Serum levels of IGFBP3 and ALS are reduced in patients with GHD or GH insensitivity". Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 25, p 959

causal:influence:pituitary_gh:positive:p.mechanism: GH directly or via IGF1 upregulates IGFBP3 expression; loss of GH action (GHD, GH insensitivity) reduces IGFBP3 levels; GH excess (acromegaly) increases IGFBP3

causal:influence:pka_activity:positive:h.evidence: Saucerman et al. 2003 J Biol Chem 278:47997 (PMID 12972422); Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology (beta-adrenergic cAMP/PKA control of chronotropy).
causal:influence:pka_activity:positive:h.mechanism: PKA phosphorylation of pacemaker and calcium-handling targets increases sinoatrial firing rate and positive chronotropy

causal:influence:plasma_2_hydroxybutyrat.evidence: Standard renal handling of filtered low-molecular-weight organic acids: Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 11th ed., Ch. 27 (excretion of freely filtered organic solutes scales with plasma concentration). Follows the model's existing plasma->urinary excretion convention.
causal:influence:plasma_2_hydroxybutyrat.mechanism: 2-hydroxybutyrate is a small freely-filtered organic acid with limited tubular reabsorption; urinary excretion is a monotone-increasing function of the filtered (plasma) load. Raising plasma 2-HB raises filtered 2-HB and thus urinary 2-HB.

causal:influence:plasma_3_ketoacyl_coa_t.evidence: GeneReviews (Long-Chain Hydroxyacyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency / Trifunctional Protein Deficiency); (NCBI Bookshelf NBK583531, Clinical Description; 'The last three [steps of beta-oxidation] are catalyzed by the mitochondrial trifunctional protein (TFP)'); “recurrent hypoketotic hypoglycemia precipitated by infection or fasting in infancy” | TFP (containing long-chain 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase) deficiency produces a hypoketotic state, so its activity positively drives ketogenesis (do(loss)->ketones down).
causal:influence:plasma_3_ketoacyl_coa_t.mechanism: long-chain 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase (MTP) activity -> completes last step of long-chain fatty-acid beta-oxidation -> supplies acetyl-CoA for hepatic ketogenesis; LoF deficiency = natural do() causing hypoketotic hypoglycemia

causal:influence:plasma_albumin:positive.evidence: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-5.2 (5.2: Passive Transport): 'Animals also have high albumin concentrations, which the liver produces, in their blood. This protein is too large to pass easily through plasma membranes and is a major factor in controlling the osmotic pressures applied to tissues.'
causal:influence:plasma_albumin:positive.mechanism: Albumin, produced by the liver and too large to cross plasma membranes easily, is the principal determinant of plasma colloid osmotic (oncotic) pressure, which opposes capillary fluid filtration into tissues.

causal:influence:plasma_biliverdin:posit.evidence: StatPearls NBK549781 (Biochemistry, Biliverdin: biliverdin is water-soluble and can be renally filtered). PMC1145080: ‘urinary excretion of isomers of biliverdin after destruction of haemoproteins in vivo’. Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (renal filtration depends on water-solubility). | intervention: do(plasma_biliverdin up) via heme oxygenase overactivation or impaired biliverdin reductase
causal:influence:plasma_biliverdin:posit.mechanism: Biliverdin is water-soluble (unlike unconjugated bilirubin) and, when present in plasma at elevated concentrations, passes freely through the glomerular filter and appears in urine. Elevated plasma biliverdin (e.g., impaired biliverdin reductase) directly drives urinary biliverdin excretion.

causal:influence:plasma_bradykinin:posit.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.17 (Local and Humoral Control of Blood Flow by the Tissues) §Bradykinin: “even smaller amounts injected locally into tissues can cause marked local edema resulting from increase in capillary pore size.”
causal:influence:plasma_bradykinin:posit.mechanism: bradykinin widens endothelial capillary pores, raising microvascular permeability

causal:influence:plasma_deoxycorticoster.evidence: "The principal difference from 21-hydroxylase deficiency is hypertension, which is thought to be secondary to the mineralocorticoid effect of DOC excess. ... Accumulation of corticosterone and DOC results in severe hypokalemic hypertension." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 15, p 535–536. Also confirmed by pharmacological reversal: "Glucocorticoid replacement reverses the DOC-induced suppression of the renin-angiotensin system and lowers blood pressure." p 307.  ||  "Excess DOC secretion eventually leads to hypertension, hypokalemic alkalosis, and suppression of the renin-angiotensin system" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 23, p 905
causal:influence:plasma_deoxycorticoster.mechanism: DOC acts as a mineralocorticoid, promoting renal sodium/water retention and raising arterial blood pressure

causal:influence:plasma_dihydrotestoster.evidence: 5-alpha-reductase type 2 deficiency (OMIM 264600) — DHT is markedly low; StatPearls NBK539904; Integrative review of SRD5A2 deficiency PMC7167369; Structure of SRD5A2 with finasteride PMC7591894 (DHT affinity for androgen receptor 2-5x testosterone); MedlinePlus Genetics SRD5A2 gene. causal:influence:plasma_dihydrotestoster.mechanism: Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) is the most potent endogenous androgen (androgen-receptor affinity ~5x testosterone), contributing directly to circulating plasma androgen concentration. causal:influence:plasma_free_fatty_acids.evidence: Mechanism: FFA up -> FAO up -> matrix acetyl-CoA up -> CrAT buffering -> acetylcarnitine export -> plasma C2 up. causal:influence:plasma_free_fatty_acids.mechanism: Plasma acetylcarnitine (C2) reflects the mitochondrial acetyl-CoA/CoA ratio: when beta-oxidation flux outpaces TCA-cycle capacity, excess acetyl-CoA is buffered by carnitine acetyltransferase (CrAT) to acetylcarnitine, which is exported to plasma. A do(increase) in plasma free fatty acids (fasting, lipolysis, exercise) drives hepatic and muscle FAO, raises matrix acetyl-CoA, and increases plasma C2. Human fasting/exercise studies show concordant FFA and plasma C2 rises with hepato-splanchnic C2 release.
